documents: Fu et al. 2022, Representation of the Mean Atlantic Subtropical Cells in CMIP6 Models, JGR Oceans 127, e2021JC018191 (published PDF, 21 pages)
pages_convention: PDF pages counted from 1 (these coincide with the printed 'n of 21' article pages)

entry.evidence: the representation of the Atlantic STCs in state-of-the-art coupled climate models has not yet been systematically investigated

steps.action: Pose the question of how well CMIP6 coupled models reproduce the mean Atlantic STCs, and how the STC components are linked across models.
steps.quote: the representation of the Atlantic STCs in state-of-the-art coupled climate models has not yet been systematically investigated

steps.action: Take observation-based STC transport estimates (Zhang et al. 2003; Tuchen et al. 2019, 2020) and earlier model estimates as the reference picture.
steps.quote: Tuchen et al. (2019) estimated the mean Atlantic STCs with a net poleward divergence of 14.6 ± 3.4 Sv

steps.action: Extract historical-run output from 28 CMIP6 models, interpolate it to 0.5°, and compute Ekman, mixed-layer, thermocline, boundary and interior transports at 10°N and 10°S and the EUC at 23°W.
steps.quote: we focus on the mean state of the Atlantic STCs by analyzing output from the “historical” simulations of 28 CMIP6 coupled models

steps.action: Assemble the observational references: Argo climatology geostrophic sections, NCEP/CFSR and ASCAT wind stress, and the 31-section shipboard ADCP mean at 23°W.
steps.quote: a mean zonal velocity section at 23°W calculated from 31 repeated shipboard ADCP sections is used to validate the modeled mean EUC

steps.action: Compute the ensemble meridional overturning streamfunction showing the two STCs and the AMOC superposition.
steps.quote: shows the shallow overturning cells (i.e., the STCs) in both hemispheres

steps.action: Compare model Ekman transports with NCEP/CFSR and ASCAT: agreement at 10°N, consistently weak southward transport at 10°S.
steps.quote: the ensemble Ekman transport at 10°S (−9.3 ± 1.7 Sv) is consistently weaker than the NCEP/CFSR (−11.2 ± 2.0 Sv)

steps.action: Attribute the weak 10°S Ekman transport to a southward-displaced South Atlantic wind stress maximum (Figure S1).
steps.quote: the ensemble maximum zonal wind stress over the South Atlantic is located further south compared to the observations

steps.action: Compare ensemble temperature, salinity and density sections at 10°N and 10°S with the Argo climatology, finding a weakened zonal density gradient at 10°S.
steps.quote: the model ensemble is substantially cooler in the western half of the basin while it is markedly warmer in the eastern half of the basin

steps.action: Attribute the fresh bias at 10°S to excessive Southern Hemisphere precipitation linked to a southward-shifted ITCZ.
steps.quote: The fresh salinity bias at 10°S may be attributed to excessive precipitation in the Southern Hemisphere

steps.action: Check the geostrophic calculation against model total velocity; they agree in the interior but lose velocity at the boundary, so total velocity is used in the thermocline.
steps.quote: the ensemble geostrophic velocity (Figure 6) and transport (not shown) agree very well with the ensemble total results

steps.action: Compare meridional velocity and cumulative mixed-layer and thermocline transports with Argo-derived geostrophy: a weak 10°N WBC and interior, and a weak interior at 10°S.
steps.quote: the ensemble northward flow in the mixed layer and thermocline is markedly weaker compared to the observations

steps.action: Invoke Schott et al. (2004): Ekman divergence is partly compensated by upper-layer geostrophic convergence that cannot reverse it.
steps.quote: the trade-winds-induced Ekman divergence is compensated by a geostrophic convergence in the upper layer

steps.action: Compare the ensemble net mixed-layer divergence and thermocline convergence with Tuchen et al. (2019) and the theoretical expectation.
steps.quote: The ensemble total mixed layer divergence is in good agreement with the observed total mixed layer divergence of 14.6 ± 3.4 Sv

steps.action: Compare the ensemble EUC at 23°W with the ADCP mean: core depth matches, but maximum speed and transport are weaker, with large inter-model spread.
steps.quote: the ensemble EUC maximum velocity is only about 0.42 m s−1, substantially weaker than the observation

steps.action: Fit inter-model correlations and regressions between Ekman divergence, mixed-layer and thermocline interior convergence and EUC, then between the EUC and hemispheric components.
steps.quote: models with stronger mean Ekman divergence tend to exhibit a stronger mixed layer geostrophic convergence

steps.action: Run an inter-model SVD of 23°W zonal velocity against tropical Atlantic wind stress; the first mode (0.48 variance) couples the EUC with the Southern Hemisphere trades.
steps.quote: the intensity of the Southern Hemisphere trade winds largely explains the inter-model spread of the EUC strength

steps.action: Attribute the weak simulated EUC and weak South Atlantic geostrophic transports to weak southeast trade winds.
steps.quote: may be attributed to the weak southeast trade winds

steps.action: Correlate AMOC strength at 10°S with STC strength, the EUC and thermocline transports: no STC-AMOC link, but a strong WBC-AMOC link.
steps.quote: We find no clear pattern in the scatter plot between the STC strength and the AMOC strength

steps.action: Report how the thermocline-AMOC correlation changes when the five models with exceptionally weak WBC are included (0.83 to 0.55).
steps.quote: Including these five models strongly reduces the inter-model correlation between the thermocline transport and the AMOC at 10°S to 0.55

steps.action: Set the 10°N WBC transport against the MIMOC-based estimate of Tuchen et al. (2019); which estimate is right is left open.
steps.quote: but closer to an estimate of about 1.0 Sv (Tuchen et al., 2019)

steps.action: Relate the biases to published CMIP6 SST-bias and EUC-source studies (Richter & Tokinaga 2020; Fratantoni et al. 2000; Hazeleger & Drijfhout 2006).
steps.quote: The temperature bias is consistent with the tropical Atlantic SST biases in the CMIP6 models reported by Richter and Tokinaga (2020).

steps.action: Add model resolution and diffusion parameterization as a further factor in EUC strength, illustrated by the HadGEM3-GC31-MM versus LL contrast.
steps.quote: model horizontal and vertical resolution as well as applied parameterizations of horizontal and vertical diffusion may also play a role in determining the EUC strength

steps.action: Compare the monthly climatology and standard deviation of Ekman divergence with NCEP/CFSR, locating the bias at 10°S in DJF/MAM and flagging poorly performing models.
steps.quote: shows large differences between the model ensemble and NCEP/CFSR in boreal winter (December to February, DJF) and spring

steps.action: Compare Ekman transport from AMIP and CMIP wind stress (Figure S3) to locate the origin of the wind bias in the coupling.
steps.quote: the CMIP wind stress at 10°S are strongly weakened when compared to their AMIP counterparts

steps.action: Repeat the ensemble and inter-model analyses over periods matching the observational records (1979-2010 and 2000-2014).
steps.quote: the conclusion of this study still hold true

steps.action: Keep the claim that the ensemble reproduces the bulk STC budget but is biased weak in Southern Hemisphere Ekman transport, interior transports and EUC, tied to the southeast trades.
steps.quote: This indicates that the model ensemble retains the bulk of the observed mean STC circulation.

No; transports are derived from model output and from observation-based geostrophic and Ekman estimates
Evaluate model skill against observations and find inter-model links
Only informal causes: southeast trade-wind bias, resolution and parameterization, AMOC coupling
No distinct predictions are derived for the rival causes
Found: an existing ensemble of 28 historical simulations, treated as realizations

tree.question: 6b
tree.answer: Yes, in effect: 28 model climatologies serve as repeated cases for inter-model regressions
Survives matched-period reanalysis, model exclusion (reported) and the AMIP comparison
Biases kept; attribution to the southeast trades kept as the best explanation

end.claim: The CMIP6 ensemble reproduces the observed net STC mixed-layer divergence, thermocline convergence and upwelling. It is biased toward weak Southern Hemisphere Ekman transport, weak interior geostrophic transports and a weak EUC, whose inter-model spread is tied to the southeast trade winds.

decisive_move.sentence: Comparing the 28-model ensemble transports and sections against NCEP/CFSR, ASCAT, Argo and ADCP observations is what establishes the biases that make up the characterization.

gates.evidence: The data are an existing CMIP6 archive analysed without a prior hypothesis. The model-observation comparisons could have shown no bias (claim partly tested), but the trade-wind attribution rests on correlations and SVD with no decisive test. Nothing is reported as fixed before the analysis.

imports.item: singular value decomposition across models (inter-model SVD)
inter-model correlation and linear regression with 95% confidence bands

novelty_claims.quote: This study provides the first assessment of the simulated Atlantic STCs in the CMIP6 models
has not yet been systematically investigated

limits: Composition is none_fits: the paper is a model-evaluation study (a capability characterization of an existing ensemble), with inter-model regressions in a natures_repetition style. It does not follow the capability_first or forecast_verification walks. Sub-claims at other statuses: the inter-model relations (Ekman divergence to convergence and EUC, WBC to AMOC, STC decoupled from AMOC) are regularity_in_range across the 28 models; the attribution of weak EUC and southern STC to the weak southeast trades is best_explanation; the salinity bias from excess precipitation and the role of resolution are hypotheses only. The paper does not report results for alternative mixed-layer criteria, section latitudes, boundary definitions or interpolation choices; the interpolation effect is asserted as marginal without being shown. The matched-period check is stated without figures or numbers. The AMIP comparison and the wind-maximum shift are in the supplement (Figures S1, S3), which was not supplied. Observational references carry their own uncertainty, and the 10°N WBC reference is unresolved (Argo versus MIMOC). It is inference that the analysis path was settled after viewing the data, since no plan is described. Small inconsistencies appear in the text (ASCAT 12.0 written without a sign; Summary 14.9 versus 14.6 Sv for Tuchen et al. 2019).

disagreements.support: The ensemble matches the observed net STC budget but shows weak Southern Hemisphere Ekman transport, weak interior geostrophic flow and a weak EUC relative to observations.
disagreements.quote: despite the discussed biases in the simulated South Atlantic trade winds, EUC, and partition between the interior and WBC parts of the thermocline

disagreements.target: Tuchen et al. (2019) choice of the 26.0 kg m−3 isopycnal as the STC lower boundary
disagreements.support: They use 26.4 kg m−3 so that the thermocline layer covers the bottom of the EUC core.
disagreements.quote: Note that this isopycnal is larger than the 26.0 kg m−3 selected by Tuchen et al. (2019).

disagreements.target: Argo-derived versus MIMOC-based (Tuchen et al., 2019) WBC estimates at 10°N
disagreements.support: The model WBC sits between the two observational estimates, and with no long-term direct WBC observation the authors cannot decide which is right.
disagreements.quote: it is difficult to conclude which estimate best represents the WBC at 10°N

alternatives_considered.chosen: 26.4 kg m−3 isopycnal as lower thermocline boundary
alternatives_considered.reason: covers the bottom of the EUC core

alternatives_considered.alternatives: atmospheric wind stress tauu (used for BCC-CSM2-MR, BCC-ESM1, MIROC6)

alternatives_considered.reason: facilitates calculations and comparisons; most models have 1° zonal resolution
